A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Star Attention work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing additions, removals, and relocated content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original RULER and BABILong evaluations, inference timings, and experiments varying anchor content, position, and size.

after.justification: V2 retains original evaluations and ablations and adds results comparing sparse attention methods on RULER and InfiniteBench.

M1.justification: Anchor-prefixed local context encoding and distributed global query attention remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1–2. V2's additional Flash Attention and TRT-LLM descriptions document implementation choices without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds ten evaluated InfiniteBench tasks in Table 3, substantially extending RULER and BABILong coverage through summarization, multilingual QA, dialogue, code debugging, and mathematical retrieval. Code.Run and Math.Calc appear only in the appendix's benchmark description and are not counted as demonstrated evaluations.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates against global/Ring Attention and includes vanilla inference timings. V2 additionally evaluates StreamingLLM and MInference on RULER and InfiniteBench, substantially broadening the actual comparator set beyond dense attention implementations.

E3.justification: V2 changes accuracy deltas from relative percentages to absolute percentage-point differences and introduces a StreamingLLM configuration with 1,000 sink tokens and an 8,000-token window. BABILong evaluation replaces Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Gradient's 1048K model. Retained sample counts, precision, GPU allocations, and block-size rules otherwise match.

E4.justification: The context-size and anchor-size sweeps, anchor position/content experiments, and RULER category analysis test the same questions under retained conditions. V1 Figures 5 and 7 become v2 Figure 5's panels; the category analysis remains in v2 Figure 7. Removed detailed benchmark scores do not constitute a separate removed ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's additional result tables retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result matrices in Tables 2–3; InfiniteBench averages are 46.51 for Star Attention, 34.07 for MInference, 14.72 for StreamingLLM, and 48.06 for full attention. It removes v1 Tables 8–18, losing exact BABILong and detailed per-task RULER scores, and changes the BABILong model results in Figure 4. Retained long-context speedups already appeared in v1; their revised accuracy deltas largely reflect the reporting-metric change.

T1.justification: The augmented-context definition, attention equations 1–4, and distributed-softmax derivation are unchanged. V2 adds no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the retained-accuracy claim from 95–100% to 97–100%, while retaining the two-phase contribution and up-to-11x speedup claim. The conclusion removes v1's additional assertion about preserving similar accuracy when scaling to 1M tokens and larger models.

C2.justification: New Section 3.3 interprets the added comparisons as evidence of generalization to real-world, instruction-heavy tasks and superiority over other sparse methods. Some statements exceed the tables' support: MInference wins at 16K and 64K on RULER and on InfiniteBench Math.Find. Existing multi-hop, anchor-size, and base-model limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies Flash Attention's use on each host and uniformly across Star/Ring implementations, discloses a TRT-LLM implementation, and provides sparse-baseline settings and InfiniteBench task statistics. Existing hardware/worker tables, prompt templates, precision, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: A rewritten introduction and new Section 5 substantially expand positioning against distributed attention, sparse inference, chunk-encoding methods, and memory optimization. Added works include MInference, Tree Attention, Writing in the Margins, E2LLM, Titans, and InfLLM; the Performers citation is removed. This extends well beyond relocating the earlier overview.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and experimental narrative, introduces a standalone related-work section, and reorganizes the appendices. Benchmark and implementation sections exchange order, while the detailed accuracy appendices are replaced by a shorter RULER analysis.

P2.justification: V2 merges the separate context-size and anchor-size plots into Figure 5, redraws category plots, and additionally visualizes the retained speed–accuracy table in Figure 6a. New comparison and benchmark-configuration tables accompany removal of extensive appendix score tables, substantially changing the document's displays and layout.

improvement.justification: The sparse-baseline comparisons and InfiniteBench evaluation address important gaps in v1's comparative evidence, and the implementation and related-work explanations improve context. However, v2 removes detailed per-task evidence and introduces blanket superiority statements contradicted by Tables 2–3, including MInference's RULER and Math.Find wins. The gains in comparative relevance coexist with reduced auditability and less accurate interpretation, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
